ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Preserve the board-first composition, but make the story relationship substantive: identify the start token explicitly as Cub in-board and place a small visible Pup at or beside the star goal. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Preserve the board as the hero but reduce the two side cards' contrast and visual mass, consolidating their essential guidance into one quieter instruction tier. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Standardize the board first: use one path stroke width, cap and junction construction; mask every path cleanly within each tile; remove detached seam fragments; and give start and goal markers the same stroke, shadow, and dimensional language. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Make Cub and the goal star bespoke illustrated tokens with stronger scale and personality, give start-to-goal progression a purposeful accent trail, and turn the help/story panels into playful in-world objects while keeping tile variation tied to path function. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Preserve the board-first composition, but make the story relationship substantive: identify the start token explicitly as Cub in-board and place a small visible Pup at or beside the star goal.—while using the clarity action—Preserve the board as the hero but reduce the two side cards' contrast and visual mass, consolidating their essential guidance into one quieter instruction tier.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
